sq.q: Explain the fundamentals of arrays and the basic operations that can be performed on arrays
answer: An array is a collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations . It allows efficient access using an index.
Index-based access (0-based indexing in most languages)
Homogeneous elements (all elements are of the same type)
Traversal : Visiting each element of the array one by one to perform some operation (e.g., printing values).
Insertion : Adding a new element at a specific position in the array. In static arrays, insertion may involve shifting elements to make space.
Deletion : Removing an element from a specific index. After deletion, the remaining elements are usually shifted to maintain the order.
Searching : Finding the location/index of a given element in the array. Linear search or binary search can be used (binary search requires the array to be sorted).
Updating : Changing the value of an existing element at a particular index.
Sorting : Arranging the elements in a specific order (ascending or descending) using algorithms like bubble sort, insertion sort, etc.
